newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. did not tell Russian leaders of Iraq plans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. did not tell Russian leaders of Iraq plans.

text.p: The Russian leadership was not informed of U.S. plans to launch air strikes on Iraq, President Boris Yeltsin's foreign affairs adviser said on Thursday.
Asked if Russia had been consulted on the U.S. action in advance, Dmitry Rurikov told a news briefing: "The Russian leadership was not informed."
Rurikov said that Russia's position on the strikes had been "sufficiently eloquently" expressed by the government and foreign ministry.

The Russian government demanded a halt to all military action against Iraq and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said the bombings could lead to "catastrophic consequences" and "anarchy" on the world scene.
Yeltsin's chief of staff Anatoly Chubais said the president saw serious complications from the attacks.
Rurikov also said that Moscow was definitely not consulted. "To talk about coordination is simply not serious."
